chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from a man, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-A'ala ibn Kamil
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Among the supplications is that which is befitting for its performer, when he forgets it, to make up for it.'

He should say after the morning (prayer): 'There is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no associates for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He causes to live and He causes to die, and He is Living and will not die. In His Hand is the goodness, all of it, and He is Able upon everything,' ten times.
And he should say: 'I seek Refuge with Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing,' ten times.
So if he forgets anything from that, it would be upon him to make up for it.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah
key_terms.يَقْضِيَهُ: To make up for it (compensate for a missed act)
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He causes to live and He causes to die

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed method for making up forgotten morning supplications in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific compensatory dhikr for missed morning remembrances, emphasizing the recitation of 'La ilaha illallah...' ten times, which encapsulates core theological attributes of divine sovereignty and power. This practice reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining spiritual continuity through structured remembrance, linking the morning and evening adhkar as a cohesive cycle of devotion. The inclusion of seeking refuge in 'Al-Sami' al-'Alim' underscores the divine attributes of hearing and knowledge, reinforcing the believer's reliance on Allah's awareness in all affairs.
